AI Summary
The Forward Deployed Engineer at NTT DATA is responsible for building and prototyping solutions for document ingestion, model gateway integration, and production automation. The role involves working both onshore and remotely, developing APIs, workflow logic, and integration components for MSIG and underwriting systems. Candidates must have at least 7 years of software engineering experience (including 4 years in offshore builds), strong Python skills, and hands-on experience with LLM applications, document processing, and cloud deployment. Familiarity with CI/CD, containerization, and infrastructure-as-code is required. The position offers a salary range of $155,700 to $259,500, depending on experience and qualifications. Preferred qualifications include experience with LLM gateway tools, multi-provider routing, and regulated financial services domains.

Req ID: 390285 

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer to join our team in Remote, New Jersey (US-NJ), United States (US).

 

Forward Deployed Engineers are the builders on this engagement. They work inside the Client environment and repositories, turning specifications into working software quickly and then hardening it for production. In design, the Spec FDEs build prototypes of submission intake and FNOL that MSIG stakeholders can use and react to. In build, the FDE team delivers the production services, integrations and automation behind both tracks.

 

Core responsibilities (all variants)

Build services, APIs and workflow logic for the model gateway and the document ingestion pipeline.
Write and maintain prompts, agent definitions and evaluators, and use evaluation results to improve extraction quality.
Implement integration components, schemas, mappings and transformation logic for delivery into MSIG underwriting and claims systems.
Contribute to CI/CD, environment configuration, test automation and release notes.
Work to specifications and the prioritized backlog, and flag early when a spec is ambiguous or unworkable.
Keep all code and artifacts in client repositories to MSIG and NTT DATA engineering standards.

 

Spec FDE focus (design, onshore)

Turn specifications into working prototypes fast, often within days, so stakeholders can validate concepts on real documents.
Iterate prototypes in the specify, prototype, validate, refine loop alongside the Domain Advisor and AI Business Analyst.
Build early extraction pipelines for D&O and Ocean Marine Cargo documents, with source-passage traceability and confidence scoring.
Stand up a working gateway prototype showing routing, fallback and cost logging.
Harden accepted prototypes into build-ready designs with clear technical specs for the build team.

 

Required qualifications

Spec and onshore build: 7+ years of software engineering; offshore build: 4+ years.
Strong Python; working knowledge of TypeScript or Java is a plus.
Hands-on experience building LLM applications: prompt engineering, tool use or agents, evaluation, RAG, and vector search.
Experience with document processing: OCR, layout-aware parsing, classification and structured extraction.
Solid API and integration skills (REST, event-driven patterns) and cloud deployment on AWS, Azure or GCP.
CI/CD, containerization and infrastructure-as-code experience.
Spec FDEs specifically: proven ability to prototype quickly and work directly with business users.

 

Preferred

Experience with LLM gateway or proxy tooling and multi-provider model routing.
Insurance, financial services or other document-heavy regulated domains.
Experience with knowledge graphs, entity resolution or temporal data models.

 

NTT DATA provides a reasonable range of compensation for U.S.-based positions. The starting pay range for this role will depend on the nature of the role offered and will either be [$155,700 - $259,500], or [$80-$100] if the role is hired as a temporary position. Actual compensation will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s relevant experience, technical skills, and other qualifications.
 
This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation based on individual and/or company performance. If the position offered in temporary, the position will not be eligible for incentive compensation.
